key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics, ferroelectrics, and low-power computing can be co-designed to power distributed AI at the edge instead of relying on centralized data centers.
engineering_relevance: The paper frames reliable local energy harvesting and ultra-low-power memory/neuromorphic hardware as the key enablers for scalable, sustainable edge computing.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaic requirements for distributed intelligence
Map how emerging materials meet energy-harvesting and storage needs
Argue for (anti)ferroelectrics in electrostatic storage and in-memory neuromorphic devices
evidence_signal: This is a perspective paper, so its evidence is a synthesis of current performance trends and materials gaps rather than new experimental benchmarking.
watch_item: A major implementation challenge is matching intermittent indoor energy generation with the power demands and reliability needs of edge AI hardware.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
